units.zh: 乾化二年正月，宣：「上元夜，任諸市及坊市各點彩燈，金吾不用禁夜。」
units.en: In the first month of Qianhua 2, the court proclaimed: "On Lantern Festival night, every market and ward may hang colored lamps; the Jinwu need not enforce the curfew."
units.literal: In the first month of Qianhua 2, an announcement stated: "On the Lantern Festival night, let every market and ward hang colored lamps; the Jinwu need not enforce the curfew."

units.zh: 近年以來，以都下聚兵太廣，未嘗令坊市點燈故也。
units.en: In recent years, with too many troops concentrated at the capital, the wards had not been allowed to light lamps—that was the reason.
units.literal: In recent years, because troops massed at the capital were too numerous, the wards had never been allowed to light lamps—that is why.

units.zh: 甲申，以時雪久愆，命丞相及三省官群望祈禱。
units.en: On jiashen, with timely snow long overdue, the Emperor ordered the chancellor and officials of the Three Departments to pray at the various altars.
units.literal: On jiashen, because timely snow had long been lacking, the chancellor and officials of the Three Departments were ordered to pray at the various altars.

units.zh: 詔曰：「謗木求規，集囊貢事，將裨理道，豈限側言。
units.en: An edict read: "The slander-wood seeks counsel; the bag gathers reports—all to aid governance. Why limit oneself to oblique speech?
units.literal: An edict stated: "The slander-wood seeks counsel; the bag gathers matters—this will aid governance; how could it be limited to oblique words?

units.zh: 應內外文武百官及草澤，並許上封事，極言得失。」
units.en: Civil and military officials within and without, and commoners alike, may submit sealed memorials and speak freely of what is right and wrong."
units.literal: All civil and military officials inside and outside, and commoners, are permitted to submit sealed memorials and speak fully of gains and losses."

units.zh: 以丁審衢為陳州，而審衢厚以鞍馬、金帛為謝恩之獻，帝慮其漁民，復其獻而停之。
units.en: Ding Shenqu was appointed prefect of Chenzhou; he sent lavish gifts of saddles, horses, and silks in thanks for the appointment. Fearing he would fleece the people, the Emperor returned the gifts and refused them.
units.literal: Ding Shenqu was appointed to Chenzhou, but Shenqu lavishly offered saddles, horses, and silks as thanks for grace; the Emperor, fearing he preyed on the people, returned the gifts and stopped him.

units.zh: 封保義節度使王檀為琅琊郡王。
units.en: Baoyi Military Commissioner Wang Tan was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya.
units.literal: Baoyi Military Commissioner Wang Tan was enfeoffed as Prince of Langya Commandery.

units.zh: 命供奉官硃嶠于河南府宣取先收禁定州進奉官崔騰並傔從一十四人，並釋放，仍命押領送至貝。
units.en: The Emperor ordered Palace Attendant Zhu Qiao to proclaim at Henan Prefecture the release of detained Dingzhou tribute officer Cui Teng and his fourteen attendants, and had them escorted to Bei.
units.literal: The Emperor ordered Palace Attendant Zhu Qiao to proclaim at Henan Prefecture the release of the detained Dingzhou tribute officer Cui Teng and fourteen attendants, and still ordered them escorted to Bei.

units.zh: 騰，唐戶部侍郎潔之子也。
units.en: He was the son of Tang Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Jie.
units.literal: Teng was the son of Tang Vice Minister of Revenue Cui Jie.

units.zh: 廣明喪亂，客于北諸侯，為定州節度使王處存所辟，去載領貢獻至闕。
units.en: During the Guangming upheaval he had lived among northern lords; Wang Chucun, military commissioner of Dingzhou, had recruited him, and the year before he had led tribute to court.
units.literal: In the Guangming turmoil he sojourned among northern lords, was recruited by Dingzhou Military Commissioner Wang Chucun, and last year led tribute to court.

units.zh: 未幾，其帥稱兵，遂縶之。
units.en: Before long his commander rebelled and had him imprisoned.
units.literal: Before long his commander raised troops and imprisoned him.

units.zh: 至是，帝念賓介之來，又已出境，特命縱而歸焉。
units.en: Now the Emperor, mindful that a guest envoy had come and had already crossed the border, specially ordered his release and return home.
units.literal: At this time the Emperor, mindful that a guest envoy had come and had already left the border, specially ordered him released and sent home.

units.zh: 丙戌，有司以孟春太廟薦享上言，命丞相杜曉攝祭行事。
units.en: On bingxu the court reported on the spring ancestral offering; the Emperor had Chancellor Du Xiao conduct the rite in his stead.
units.literal: On bingxu the authorities memorialized on the first-spring offering at the Imperial Ancestral Temple; the Emperor ordered Chancellor Du Xiao to perform the rites as proxy.

units.zh: 丙申夕，熒惑犯房第二星。
units.en: On the night of bingshen, Mars encroached on the second star of the Fang asterism.
units.literal: On the night of bingshen, Mars trespassed the second star of Fang.

units.zh: 二月庚戌，中和節，御崇勳殿，召丞相、大學士、河南尹，略封訖，于萬春門外廡賜以酒食。
units.en: On gengxu in the second month, the Zhonghe Festival, the Emperor presided at Chongxun Hall, summoned the chancellor, Grand Academicians, and Henan Intendant; after the brief audience he bestowed food and drink in the corridor outside Wanchun Gate.
units.literal: On gengxu in the second month, the Zhonghe Festival, the Emperor presided at Chongxun Hall, summoned the chancellor, Grand Academicians, and Henan Intendant, finished the brief audience, and bestowed food and drink in the corridor outside Wanchun Gate.

units.zh: 《五代會要》，二月，追封故魏博節度使羅宏信為趙王。
units.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the second month the court posthumously enfeoffed the late Weibo commissioner Luo Hongxin as Prince of Zhao.
units.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the second month the late Weibo Military Commissioner Luo Hongxin was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

units.zh: 癸丑，敕曰：「今載春寒頗甚，雨澤仍愆，司天監占以夏秋必多霖潦，宜令所在郡縣告喻百姓，備淫雨之患。」
units.en: On guichou an order read: "This year spring cold is severe and rain still lacking; the Directorate of Astronomy divines heavy rains in summer and autumn—let every prefecture and county warn the people to prepare for floods."
units.literal: On guichou an order stated: "This year spring cold is quite severe and rain still lacking; the Directorate of Astronomy divines that summer and autumn will see much flood—let every prefecture and county inform the people to guard against excessive rain."

units.zh: 庚申，禦宣威殿開宴，丞相洎文武官屬咸被召列侍，竟日而罷。
units.en: On gengshen the Emperor held a banquet at Xuanwei Hall; the chancellor and all civil and military officials were summoned to attend in rows until evening.
units.literal: On gengshen the Emperor held a banquet at Xuanwei Hall; the chancellor and civil and military officials were all summoned to attend in rows until day’s end.

units.zh: 壬戌，帝將巡按北境，中外戒嚴，詔以河南尹、守中書令、判六軍事張宗奭為大內留守。
units.en: On renxu, as the Emperor prepared to inspect the northern border, court and realm went on alert; Zhang Zongshi, Henan intendant, keeper of the Secretariat, and director of the Six Armies, was named Grand Inner Custodian.
units.literal: On renxu the Emperor was about to tour the northern frontier; court and country were placed on alert; an edict appointed Henan Intendant, Keeper of the Secretariat, and Director of the Six Armies Zhang Zongshi Grand Inner Custodian.

units.zh: 中書門下奏，差定文武官領務尤切宜扈駕者三十八人。
units.en: The Secretariat memorialized, naming thirty-eight civil and military officials whose duties were especially urgent and who should attend the imperial progress.
units.literal: The Secretariat memorialized, fixing thirty-eight civil and military officials whose duties were especially urgent and who should attend the imperial progress.

units.zh: 詔工部尚書李皎、左散騎常侍孫騭、右諫議大夫張衍、兵部侍郎劉邈、兵部郎中張俊、光祿少卿盧秉彝並令扈蹕。
units.en: By edict Li Jiao, minister of works, Sun Zhi, left regular attendant, Zhang Yan, right remonstrator, Liu Miao, vice minister of war, Zhang Jun, war bureau director, and Lu Bingyi, vice director of imperial sacrifices, were all ordered on the progress.
units.literal: An edict ordered Minister of Works Li Jiao, Left Regular Attendant Sun Zhi, Right Remonstrance Official Zhang Yan, Vice Minister of War Liu Miao, War Bureau Director Zhang Jun, and Vice Director of Imperial Sacrifices Lu Bingyi all to attend the progress.

units.zh: 甲子，發自洛師，夕次河陽。
units.en: On jiazi he left Luoyang and stopped at Heyang that night.
units.literal: On jiazi he set out from Luoyang and halted at Heyang that evening.

units.zh: 《通鑒》云：至白馬屯，賜從官食，多未至，遣騎趣之于路。
units.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Reaching Baima Station, he bestowed food on attending officials; many had not arrived, and he sent riders to hurry them along the road.
units.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》 says: Reaching Baima Station, he bestowed food on attending officials; many had not arrived, and he sent riders to hurry them on the road.

units.zh: 左散騎常侍孫騭、右諫議大夫張衍、兵部郎中張俊最後至，帝命撲殺之。
units.en: Sun Zhi, Zhang Yan, and Zhang Jun came late; the Emperor had them beaten to death.
units.literal: Left Regular Attendant Sun Zhi, Right Remonstrance Official Zhang Yan, and War Bureau Director Zhang Jun arrived last; the Emperor ordered them beaten to death.

units.zh: 乙丑，次溫縣。
units.en: On yichou he stopped at Wen County.
units.literal: On yichou he halted at Wen County.

units.zh: 丙寅，次武陟。
units.en: On bingyin he stopped at Wuzhi.
units.literal: On bingyin he halted at Wuzhi.

units.zh: 懷州刺史段明遠迎拜於境上，其內外所備，咸豐霈焉。
units.en: Duan Mingyuan, inspector of Huai Prefecture, met him at the border with obeisance; supplies within and without were lavish beyond measure.
units.literal: Huai Prefecture Inspector Duan Mingyuan met and bowed at the border; all provisions inside and out were abundantly lavish.

units.zh: 丁卯，次獲嘉。
units.en: On dingmao he stopped at Huojia.
units.literal: On dingmao he halted at Huojia.

units.zh: 戊辰，次衛州之新鄉。
units.en: On wuchen he stopped at Xinxiang in Weizhou.
units.literal: On wuchen he halted at Xinxiang in Weizhou.

units.zh: 己巳，晨發衛州，夕止淇門，內衙十將使以十指揮兵士至於行在。
units.en: On jisi he left Weizhou in the morning and camped at Qimen that evening; Inner Palace Ten Generals marched their commands to the imperial camp.
units.literal: On jisi he set out from Weizhou in the morning and halted at Qimen in the evening; Inner Palace Ten Generals led soldiers by the tens to the imperial camp.

units.zh: 辛未，駐蹕黎陽。
units.en: On xinwei he encamped at Liyang.
units.literal: On xinwei he halted at Liyang.

units.zh: 癸酉，發自黎陽，夕次內黃。
units.en: On guiyou he left Liyang and camped at Neihuang that night.
units.literal: On guiyou he set out from Liyang and halted at Neihuang that evening.

units.zh: 甲戌，次昌樂縣。
units.en: On jiaxu he stopped at Changle County.
units.literal: On jiaxu he halted at Changle County.

units.zh: 丁丑，次於永濟縣。
units.en: On dingchou he stopped at Yongji County.
units.literal: On dingchou he halted at Yongji County.

units.zh: 青州節度使賀德倫奏，統領兵士赴曆亭軍前。
units.en: He Delun, Qingzhou commissioner, reported that he was marching his forces to Liting.
units.literal: Qingzhou Military Commissioner He Delun memorialized that he was leading troops to the front at Liting.

units.zh: 戊寅，至貝州，命四丞相及學士李琪、盧文度、知制誥竇賞等十五人扈從，其左常侍韋戩等二十三人止焉。
units.en: On wuyin he reached Beizhou and ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend; Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained behind.
units.literal: On wuyin he reached Beizhou, ordered the four chancellors and Academicians Li Qi, Lu Wendu, Drafter Dou Shang, and fifteen others to attend, while Left Regular Attendant Wei Zhan and twenty-three others remained.

units.zh: 己卯，發自貝州，夕駐蹕於野落。
units.en: On jimao he set out from Beizhou and camped that evening in the open country.
units.literal: On jimao he set out from Beizhou and halted that evening in the open country.

units.zh: 三月庚辰朔，次於棗強縣之西城。
units.en: On gengchen, the first of the third month, he halted at the west city of Zaoqiang County.
units.literal: On the first day of the third month, gengchen, he halted at the west city of Zaoqiang County.

units.zh: 《通鑒》：辛巳，至下博南，登觀津塚。
units.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On xinsi he came to south of Xiabo and ascended Guanjin Mound.
units.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On xinsi he reached south of Xiabo and climbed Guanjin Mound.

units.zh: 趙將符暕引數百騎巡邏，不知是帝，遽前逼之。
units.en: Zhao general Fu Yan led several hundred horsemen on patrol, did not recognize the Emperor, and suddenly pressed forward.
units.literal: Zhao general Fu Yan led several hundred horsemen on patrol, did not know it was the Emperor, and suddenly pressed forward.

units.zh: 或告曰：「晉兵大至矣！」
units.en: Someone cried: "Jin troops are upon us in force!"
units.literal: Someone reported: "Jin troops have arrived in great numbers!"

units.zh: 帝行幄，亟引兵趣棗強，與楊師厚軍合。
units.en: The Emperor quit his camp, hurried his troops toward Zaoqiang, and united with Yang Shihou's army.
units.literal: The Emperor left his traveling pavilion, hastily led troops toward Zaoqiang, and joined Yang Shihou’s army.

units.zh: 丙戌，鎮、定諸軍招討使楊師厚奏下棗強縣，車駕即日疾馳南還。
units.en: On bingxu Zhen and Ding Pacification Commissioner Yang Shihou memorialized that Zaoqiang County had fallen; the imperial carriage galloped south that same day.
units.literal: On bingxu Zhen and Ding Pacification Commissioner Yang Shihou memorialized that Zaoqiang County had fallen; the imperial carriage that day galloped south.

units.zh: 丁亥，復至貝州。
units.en: On dinghai he was back at Beizhou.
units.literal: On dinghai he returned to Beizhou.

units.zh: 庚寅，楊師厚與副招討李周彝等准詔來朝。
units.en: On gengyin Yang Shihou, deputy pacifier Li Zhouyi, and others presented themselves at court by edict.
units.literal: On gengyin Yang Shihou and Deputy Pacifier Li Zhouyi and others came to court as ordered.

units.zh: 辛卯，詔丞相、翰林六學士、文武從官、都招討使及諸軍統指揮使等，賜食於行殿。
units.en: On xinmao an edict ordered the chancellor, Hanlin Six Academicians, civil and military attendants, Grand Pacification Commissioner, and unified army commanders to be feasted at the traveling hall.
units.literal: On xinmao an edict ordered the chancellor, Hanlin Six Academicians, civil and military attendants, Grand Pacification Commissioner, and unified army commanders to be given food at the traveling hall.

units.zh: 壬辰，命以羊酒等各賜從官。
units.en: On renchen he had mutton and wine distributed to each attending official.
units.literal: On renchen he ordered mutton and wine given separately to attending officials.

units.zh: 甲午，幸貝州之東闉閱武。
units.en: On jiawu he went to Beizhou's east gate to review the army.
units.literal: On jiawu he visited the east gate of Beizhou to review troops.

units.zh: 乙未，帝復幸東闉閱騎軍。
units.en: On yiwei he again went to the east gate to review the cavalry.
units.literal: On yiwei the Emperor again visited the east gate to review the cavalry.

units.zh: 敕以攻下棗強縣有功將校杜暉等一十一人，並超加檢校官，衙官宋彥等二十五人並超授軍職。
units.en: An order promoted eleven officers distinguished in taking Zaoqiang, including Du Hui, with supernumerary inspector ranks, and gave twenty-five yamen officers including Song Yan higher military posts.
units.literal: An order stated that eleven meritorious officers in the capture of Zaoqiang County, including Du Hui, were all given supernumerary inspector ranks, and twenty-five yamen officers including Song Yan were all promoted in military office.

units.zh: 丙午，次濟源縣。
units.en: On bingwu he stopped at Jiyuan County.
units.literal: On bingwu he halted at Jiyuan County.

units.zh: 詔曰：「淑律將遷，亢陽頗甚，宜令魏州差官祈禱龍潭。」
units.en: An edict read: "The harmonious pitch is about to shift and drought is severe—let Weizhou dispatch officials to pray at Dragon Pool."
units.literal: An edict stated: "The harmonious pitch is about to shift and drought yang is quite severe—let Weizhou dispatch officials to pray at Dragon Pool."

units.zh: 戊申，詔曰：「雨澤愆期，祈禱未應，宜令宰臣各于魏州靈祠精加祈禱。」
units.en: On wushen an edict read: "Rain is overdue and prayers unanswered—let each chancellor pray with utmost care at the spirit shrines of Weizhou."
units.literal: On wushen an edict stated: "Rain is overdue and prayers unanswered—let each chancellor at Weizhou spirit shrines pray with utmost care."

units.zh: 《五代會要》：三月，詔曰：「夫隆興邦國，必本於人民；
units.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the third month an edict read: "To uplift a state one must be rooted in the people;
units.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the third month an edict stated: "To uplift a state must be rooted in the people;

units.zh: 惠養疲羸，凡資於令長。
units.en: nurturing the exhausted and feeble falls wholly to local magistrates.
units.literal: to nurture the weary and weak depends entirely on magistrates.

units.zh: 苟選求之逾濫，固撫理之乖違。
units.en: If appointments are excessive, governance will surely go astray.
units.literal: If selection is excessive, governance will surely go astray.

units.zh: 如聞吏部擬官，中書除授，或緣親舊所請，或為勢要所幹，姑徇私情，靡求才實，念茲蠹弊，宜舉條章。
units.en: We hear that appointments proposed by the Ministry of Personnel and confirmed by the Secretariat often follow kin or patrons, favor private ties over merit—this abuse must be met with clear rules.
units.literal: We hear that when the Ministry of Personnel proposes offices and the Secretariat appoints, sometimes through kin and friends’ requests, sometimes through powerful men’s intercession—they indulge private feeling and do not seek real talent; mindful of this corruption, regulations should be promulgated.

units.zh: 今後應中書用人及吏部注擬，並宜省籓身之才業，驗為政之否臧，必有可觀，方可任用。
units.en: Hereafter for Secretariat appointments and Ministry nominations, all should examine the candidate’s talent and verify whether his governance was good or bad—only if there is merit may he be employed.
units.literal: Hereafter for Secretariat appointments and Ministry nominations, all should examine the candidate’s talent and verify whether his governance was good or bad—only if there is something to be seen may he be employed.

units.zh: 如或尚行請說，猶假貨財，其所司人吏，必當推窮，重加懲斷。」
units.en: Should solicitation or bribery continue, responsible officials are to investigate fully and punish without mercy."
units.literal: If anyone still practices solicitation or lends goods and money, the responsible clerks must be thoroughly investigated and punished severely."

units.zh: 四月己酉，幸魏州。
units.en: On jiyou in the fourth month he went to Weizhou.
units.literal: On jiyou in the fourth month he visited Weizhou.

units.zh: 金波亭，賜宴宰臣、文武官及六學士。
units.en: At Jinbo Pavilion he feasted the chancellors, the civil and military officials, and the Six Academicians.
units.literal: At Jinbo Pavilion he gave a feast to chancellors, civil and military officials, and the Six Academicians.

units.zh: 甲寅夕，月掩心大星。
units.en: On jiayin night the moon occulted the great star of Heart.
units.literal: On the night of jiayin the moon occulted the great star of Heart.

units.zh: 丙辰，敕：「近者星辰違度，式在修禳，宜令兩京及宋州、魏州取此月至五月禁斷屠宰。
units.en: On bingchen an order read: "Recently the stars have gone out of their courses—rectification lies in ritual prayer; let the two capitals and Songzhou and Weizhou from this month through the fifth month forbid slaughter.
units.literal: On bingchen an order stated: "Recently the stars have gone out of their courses—rectification lies in ritual prayer; let the two capitals and Songzhou and Weizhou from this month through the fifth month forbid slaughter.

units.zh: 仍各於佛寺開建道場，以迎福應。」
units.en: Let each also establish ritual platforms at Buddhist temples to welcome blessings."
units.literal: Still let each establish ritual platforms at Buddhist temples to welcome blessings."

units.zh: 己未，次黎陽縣。
units.en: On jiwei he stopped at Liyang County.
units.literal: On jiwei he halted at Liyang County.

units.zh: 《通鑒》：乙卯，博王友文來朝，請帝還東都。
units.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On yimao the Prince of Bo, Youwen, attended court and urged the Emperor to return east.
units.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On yimao Prince of Bo Youwen came to court and asked the Emperor to return to the Eastern Capital.

units.zh: 丁巳，發魏州。
units.en: On dingsi he departed Weizhou.
units.literal: On dingsi he set out from Weizhou.

units.zh: 己未，至黎陽，以疾淹留。
units.en: On jiwei he came to Liyang and stayed on, held up by sickness.
units.literal: On jiwei he reached Liyang and lingered there because of illness.

units.zh: 東都留守官吏奉表起居，賜丞相、從官酒食有差。
units.en: Custodian officials at the Eastern Capital sent memorials of greeting; chancellor and attendants received graded gifts of food and drink.
units.literal: Eastern Capital custodian officials presented memorials of inquiry; the chancellor and attending officials were given food and drink in varying measure.

units.zh: 己巳，至東都，博王友文以新創食殿上言，並進準備內宴錢三千貫、銀器一千五百兩。
units.en: On jisi he arrived at the Eastern Capital; Prince of Bo Youwen reported on the new Dining Hall and presented three thousand strings of cash and fifteen hundred taels of silver for an inner banquet.
units.literal: On jisi he reached the Eastern Capital; Prince of Bo Youwen memorialized on the newly built Dining Hall and also presented three thousand strings of cash and fifteen hundred taels of silverware prepared for an inner banquet.

units.zh: 辛未，宴於食殿，召丞相及文武從官等侍焉。
units.en: On xinwei he banqueted at the Dining Hall and summoned the chancellor and civil and military attendants to attend.
units.literal: On xinwei he banqueted at the Dining Hall and summoned the chancellor and civil and military attendants to serve.

units.zh: 帝泛九曲池，御舟傾，帝墮溺于池中，宮女侍官扶持登岸，驚悸久之。
units.en: The Emperor rowed on Nine-Bend Pool; the imperial boat capsized and he fell into the water; palace women and attendants helped him ashore, and he remained shaken for a long time.
units.literal: The Emperor rowed on Nine-Bend Pool; the imperial boat capsized and the Emperor fell into the pool; palace women and attending officials supported him ashore, and he was shaken for a long time.

units.zh: 制加建昌宮使、金紫光祿大夫、檢校司徒、開封尹、博王友文為特進、檢校太保，兼開封尹，依前建昌宮使，充東都留守。
units.en: By order Youwen, Prince of Bo, Jianchang palace commissioner, golden-seal grand master of splendid happiness, honorary grand mentor, and Kaifeng intendant, was raised to special court attendance and honorary grand guardian, kept Kaifeng intendant, and remained Jianchang commissioner and Eastern Capital custodian.
units.literal: An order advanced Jianchang Palace Commissioner, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, Honorary Grand Mentor, Kaifeng Intendant, and Prince of Bo Youwen to Special Court Attendance and Honorary Grand Guardian, also Kaifeng Intendant, continuing as Jianchang Palace Commissioner and Eastern Capital Custodian.

units.zh: 戊寅，車駕發自東京，夕次中牟縣。
units.en: On wuyin the imperial train left the Eastern Capital and camped at Zhongmou that evening.
units.literal: On wuyin the imperial carriage set out from the Eastern Capital and halted at Zhongmou County that evening.

units.zh: 五月己卯朔，從官文武自丞相而下，並詣行殿起居，親王及諸道籓帥咸奉表來上。
units.en: On jimao, the first of the fifth month, civil and military attendants from the chancellor down all came to the traveling hall for inquiry; princes and military commissioners of every circuit presented memorials.
units.literal: On the first day of the fifth month, jimao, civil and military attendants from the chancellor down all came to the traveling hall for inquiry; princes and military commissioners of every circuit presented memorials.

units.zh: 庚辰，發自鄭州，至滎陽，河南尹魏王宗奭望塵迎拜；
units.en: On gengchen he set out from Zhengzhou and reached Xingyang; Henan Intendant Prince of Wei Zongshi met him bowing in the dust;
units.literal: On gengchen he set out from Zhengzhou, reached Xingyang; Henan Intendant Prince of Wei Zongshi met him bowing in the dust;

units.zh: 河陽留後邵贊、懷州刺史段明遠等邐迤來迎。
units.en: Shao Zan, acting Heyang commissioner, Duan Mingyuan of Huai, and others met him in turn along the route.
units.literal: Heyang Acting Commissioner Shao Zan, Huai Prefecture Inspector Duan Mingyuan, and others came in succession to meet.

units.zh: 夕次汜水縣，帝召魏王宗奭入對，便於御前賜食，數刻乃退。
units.en: That night he stopped at Sishui; the Emperor called Prince of Wei Zongshi to audience, fed him before the throne, and after some time sent him away.
units.literal: That evening he halted at Sishui County; the Emperor summoned Prince of Wei Zongshi to audience and at once bestowed food before the throne; after several quarters he withdrew.

units.zh: 壬午，駐蹕于汜水，宰臣、河南尹、六學士並于內殿起居，敕以建昌宮事委宰臣於兢領之。
units.en: On renwu he was at Sishui; chancellors, the Henan intendant, and the Six Academicians attended in the inner hall; Jianchang Palace business was placed in Chancellor Yu Jing's hands.
units.literal: On renwu he halted at Sishui; chancellors, Henan Intendant, and Six Academicians all made inquiry in the inner hall; an order entrusted Jianchang Palace affairs to Chancellor Yu Jing.

units.zh: 《五代會要》：其年六月，廢建昌宮，以河南尹、魏王張宗奭為國計使，凡天下金穀兵戎舊隸建昌宮者，悉主之。
units.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the sixth month Jianchang Palace was abolished and Prince of Wei Zhang Zongshi, Henan intendant, became state comptroller, taking over all grain, funds, and troops formerly held by the palace.
units.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: In the sixth month of that year Jianchang Palace was abolished; Henan Intendant Prince of Wei Zhang Zongshi was made State Comptroller; all realm grain, funds, and troops formerly under Jianchang Palace were placed under him.

units.zh: 癸未，帝發自汜水，宣令邵贊、段明遠各歸所理。
units.en: On guawei he left Sishui and announced that Shao Zan and Duan Mingyuan should each return to their posts.
units.literal: On guawei the Emperor set out from Sishui and proclaimed that Shao Zan and Duan Mingyuan should each return to their jurisdictions.

units.zh: 午憩任村屯，夕次孝義宮。
units.en: He rested at Rencun Station at noon and lodged at Xiaoyi Palace that evening.
units.literal: At noon he rested at Rencun Station; that evening he halted at Xiaoyi Palace.

units.zh: 留都文武禮部尚書孔續而下道左迎拜。
units.en: Civil and military officials left in the capital, from Minister of Rites Kong Xu down, lined the road to welcome him.
units.literal: Capital custodian civil and military officials from Minister of Rites Kong Xu down met and bowed on the left of the road.

units.zh: 次偃師。
units.en: He stopped at Yanshi.
units.literal: He halted at Yanshi.

units.zh: 甲申，至都，文武臣奉迎於東郊。
units.en: On jiashen he entered the capital; civil and military officials received him at the eastern suburb.
units.literal: On jiashen he reached the capital; civil and military officials welcomed him at the eastern suburb.

units.zh: 渤海遣使朝貢。
units.en: Bohai presented tribute envoys.
units.literal: Bohai sent envoys with tribute.

units.zh: 宰臣薛貽矩抱恙在假，不克扈從，宣問旁午，仍命且駐東京以俟良愈。
units.en: Chancellor Xue Yiju was ill on leave and could not join the tour; the Emperor's inquiries came often, yet ordered him to stay at the Eastern Capital until recovery.
units.literal: Chancellor Xue Yiju was ill on leave and could not attend the progress; inquiries were frequent, and he was still ordered to remain at the Eastern Capital until fully recovered.

units.zh: 及薨，帝震悼頗久，命雒苑使曹守璫往弔祭之，又命輟六日、七日、八日朝參，丞相、文武並詣上閣門進名奉慰。
units.en: At his death the Emperor mourned at length, sent Luoyuan commissioner Cao Shoudang to condole, and cancelled court for the sixth through eighth; chancellor and officials filed condolence at the Upper Gate.
units.literal: When he died the Emperor mourned a long while, ordered Luoyuan Commissioner Cao Shoucong to go offer condolences, and also ordered court attendance suspended on the sixth, seventh, and eighth; chancellor and civil and military officials all went to the Upper Gate to enter their names in condolence.

units.zh: 丁亥，以彗星謫見，詔兩京見禁囚徒大辟罪以下，遞減一等，限三日內疏理訖聞奏。
units.en: On dinghai, after a comet appeared, an edict reduced by one grade the sentences of all prisoners in both capitals down through capital offenses, requiring review within three days.
units.literal: On dinghai, because a comet had appeared, an edict ordered that in the two capitals all imprisoned convicts down from capital crimes should have their sentences reduced one grade, with review completed and reported within three days.

units.zh: 《五代會要》：彗星見於靈台之西，至五月始降赦宥罪，以答天譴。
units.en: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: A comet showed west of Lingtai; not until the fifth month did the court grant amnesty for crimes to answer Heaven's reproof.
units.literal: 《Five Dynasties Huiyao》: A comet appeared west of Lingtai; only in the fifth month was an amnesty granted for crimes, to answer Heaven’s reproof.

units.zh: 又云：五月壬戌夜，熒惑犯心大星，去心四度，順行。
units.en: It adds: On renxu night in the fifth month Mars crossed the great star of Heart, four degrees off, moving direct.
units.literal: It also says: On the night of renxu in the fifth month Mars trespassed the great star of Heart, four degrees from Heart, moving direct.

units.zh: 司天奏：「大星為帝王之星，宜修省以答天譴。」
units.en: The directorate reported: "The great star is the sovereign's star—the ruler should cultivate virtue to answer Heaven's reproof."
units.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy memorialized: "The great star is the star of the Son of Heaven—self-cultivation is fitting to answer Heaven’s reproof."

units.zh: 詔曰：「生育之人，爰當暑月，乳哺之愛，方及薰風。
units.en: An edict read: "Living creatures are now in the summer months; the love of suckling meets the warm breeze.
units.literal: An edict stated: "Living creatures are now in the summer months; the love of suckling meets the warm breeze.

units.zh: 儻肆意于刲屠，豈推恩於長養，俾無殄暴，以助發生。
units.en: Wanton slaughter cannot square with nurturing life; let killing cease that growth may flourish.
units.literal: If one recklessly slaughters, how can one extend kindness in nurturing—let there be no extermination, to aid generation.

units.zh: 宜令兩京及諸州府，夏季內禁斷屠宰及採捕。
units.en: The two capitals and all prefectures and circuits shall forbid slaughter and hunting for the summer.
units.literal: Let the two capitals and every prefecture and circuit forbid slaughter and hunting through the summer.

units.zh: 天民之窮，諒由賦分；
units.en: The people's want surely lies in fate's decree;
units.literal: The people’s poverty is surely from allotted fate;

units.zh: 國章所在，亦務興仁。
units.en: yet where the state's charge rests, benevolence must still be practiced.
units.literal: where the state’s regulations lie, one must also practice benevolence.

units.zh: 所在鰥寡孤獨、廢疾不濟者，委長吏量加賑恤。
units.en: Where widowers, orphans, the solitary poor, the disabled, and the destitute are found, let chief officials give relief as needed.
units.literal: Wherever widowers, orphans, the solitary, the disabled, and those in distress are found, commission the chief official to grant relief as appropriate.

units.zh: 史載葬枯，用彰軫恤；
units.en: History praises burying the unburied dead as proof of compassion;
units.literal: History records burying the withered, to show compassion;

units.zh: 禮稱掩骼，將致和平。
units.en: ritual demands covering bleached bones to restore peace.
units.literal: ritual speaks of covering exposed bones, to bring peace.

units.zh: 應兵戈之地，有暴露骸骨，委所在長吏差人專攻收瘞。
units.en: Where war has left exposed bones, commission the local chief official to send men to gather and bury them.
units.literal: Where war has left exposed bones, commission the local chief official to send men specially to gather and bury them.

units.zh: 國癘之文，尚標七祀；
units.en: State plague ordinances still prescribe the seven sacrifices;
units.literal: The state’s plague texts still mark the seven sacrifices;

units.zh: 良藥之市，亦載三醫。
units.en: the registry of fine medicines still lists three doctors.
units.literal: the market of good medicines also records three physicians.

units.zh: 用憐無告之人，宜征有喜之術。
units.en: Pity those with none to speak for them—let skilled physicians be sought.
units.literal: Out of pity for those with no one to plead for them, skilled healing should be sought.

units.zh: 凡有疫之處，委長吏檢尋醫方，于要路曉示。
units.en: Wherever plague appears, commission the chief official to search out medical formulas and post them at key roads.
units.literal: Wherever plague appears, commission the chief official to search out medical formulas and proclaim them at key roads.

units.zh: 如有家無骨肉兼困窮不濟者，即仰長吏差醫給藥救療之。」
units.en: If any household lacks kin and is destitute and in distress, the chief official should dispatch a physician to give medicine and treat them."
units.literal: If any household lacks kin and is also destitute and in distress, the chief official should dispatch a physician to give medicine and treat them."

units.zh: 辛卯，詔曰：「亢陽滋甚，農事已傷，宜令宰臣於兢赴中嶽，杜曉赴西嶽，精切祈禱。
units.en: On xinmao an edict read: "Drought grows severe and farming is already harmed—let Chancellor Yu Jing go to the Central Peak and Du Xiao to the Western Peak for earnest prayer.
units.literal: On xinmao an edict stated: "Drought yang grows severe and farming is already harmed—let Chancellor Yu Jing go to the Central Peak and Du Xiao to the Western Peak for earnest prayer.

units.zh: 其近京靈廟，宜委河南尹，五帝壇、風師雨師、九宮貴神，委中書各差官祈之。」
units.en: Shrines near the capital were left to the Henan intendant; the Five Emperors Altar, Wind Master, Rain Master, and Nine Palaces spirits each received Secretariat officers to pray."
units.literal: Spirit shrines near the capital should be entrusted to the Henan Intendant; the Five Emperors Altar, Wind Master, Rain Master, and Nine Palaces Noble Spirits should each have officials dispatched by the Secretariat to pray."

units.zh: 《通鑒》：閏月壬戌，帝疾甚，謂近臣曰：「我經營天下三十年，不意太原餘孽更昌熾如此！
units.en: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On renxu of the intercalary month the Emperor was gravely ill; he said to his intimates: "Thirty years I have ruled, and never thought the Taiyuan remnant would grow so strong!
units.literal: 《Comprehensive Mirror》: On renxu in the intercalary month the Emperor’s illness was grave; he told close ministers: "I have managed the realm for thirty years and did not expect the Taiyuan remnant to flourish so!

units.zh: 吾觀其志不小，天復奪我年，我死，諸兒非彼敵也，吾無葬地矣！」
units.en: Their aim is not small; Heaven again cuts my years—when I die my sons cannot stand against them; I have no grave prepared!"
units.literal: I see their ambition is no small thing; Heaven again shortens my years—when I die my sons are no match for them; I have no burial ground!"

units.zh: 因哽咽，絕而復蘇。
units.en: He sobbed until breath failed, then came back.
units.literal: He choked with sobs, stopped breathing, and revived.

units.zh: 帝長子郴王友裕早卒。
units.en: His eldest son, Prince of Chen Youyu, had died young.
units.literal: The Emperor’s eldest son Prince of Chen Youyu had died early.

units.zh: 次假子友文，帝特愛之，常留守東都，兼建昌宮使。
units.en: Next came the adopted son Youwen, the Emperor's favorite, who often stayed at the Eastern Capital as Jianchang palace commissioner.
units.literal: Next was the adopted son Youwen, whom the Emperor especially loved; he often remained at the Eastern Capital as Jianchang Palace Commissioner.

units.zh: 次郢王友珪，其母亳州營倡也，為左右控鶴都指揮使。
units.en: Next was Prince of Ying Yougui, born of a Bozhou camp singer, commander of the left and right Crane-Controlled Armies.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Ying Yougui, whose mother was a camp entertainer from Bozhou; he was Commander of the Left and Right Crane-Controlled Armies.

units.zh: 次均王友貞，為東都馬步都指揮使。
units.en: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, commander of horse and foot at the Eastern Capital.
units.literal: Next was Prince of Jun Youzhen, Eastern Capital Horse and Foot Commander.

units.zh: 帝雖未以友文為太子，意常屬之。
units.en: Youwen was not named crown prince, yet the Emperor's heart was often set on him.
units.literal: Although the Emperor had not made Youwen crown prince, his intent often rested on him.

units.zh: 六月丁丑朔，帝命敬翔出友珪為萊州刺史，即命之官。
units.en: On dingchou, the first of the sixth month, the Emperor ordered Jing Xiang to issue an order posting Yougui as prefect of Laizhou, and at once ordered him to take office.
units.literal: On dingchou, the first day of the sixth month, the Emperor ordered Jing Xiang to issue an order posting Yougui as prefect of Laizhou, and at once ordered him to take office.

units.zh: 已宣旨，未行敕。
units.en: The choice had been announced, but no edict had followed.
units.literal: The intent had been proclaimed but the edict had not yet been issued.

units.zh: 時左遷者多追賜死，友珪益恐。
units.en: Many recently demoted men were hunted down and forced to die; Yougui's fear deepened.
units.literal: At that time many demoted officials were pursued and granted death; Yougui grew more fearful.

units.zh: 戊寅，友珪易服微行入 左龍虎軍，見統軍韓勍，以情告之。
units.en: On wuyin Yougui went in disguise to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, confided in commander Han Qin, and laid bare his fear.
units.literal: On wuyin Yougui changed clothes and went in secret to the Left Dragon-Tiger Army, saw Commander-in-Chief Han Qin, and told him his plight.

units.zh: 勍亦見功臣宿將多以小過被誅，懼不自保，遂相與合謀。
units.en: Qin too had seen meritorious officers killed for trifles and feared for himself; they took counsel together.
units.literal: Qin also saw meritorious generals and veteran officers often executed for small faults and feared he could not preserve himself; they then plotted together.

units.zh: 勍以牙兵五百人從友珪雜控鶴士入，伏於禁中；
units.en: Qin brought five hundred guardsmen; Yougui mixed them with the Crane-Controlled troops and hid them inside the palace;
units.literal: Qin led five hundred guardsmen to follow Yougui mixed among the Crane-Controlled troops into the palace; they lay in ambush within the forbidden precinct;

units.zh: 夜斬關入，至寢殿，侍疾者皆散走。
units.en: At night they forced the gate and reached the sleeping hall; attendants scattered.
units.literal: At night they broke through the gate and reached the sleeping hall; those attending the sick all fled.

units.zh: 帝驚起，問：「反者為誰？」
units.en: The Emperor roused himself and cried: "Who rebels?"
units.literal: The Emperor started up and asked: "Who are the rebels?"

units.zh: 友珪曰：「非他人也。」
units.en: Yougui said: "No other."
units.literal: Yougui said: "It is no other."

units.zh: 帝曰：「我固疑此賊，恨不早殺之。
units.en: The Emperor said: "I long suspected this villain—only regret I did not kill him sooner.
units.literal: The Emperor said: "I always suspected this villain—regret I did not kill him sooner.

units.zh: 汝悖逆如此，天地豈容汝乎！」
units.en: You rebel thus—Heaven and Earth will not bear you!"
units.literal: You are so rebellious—how could Heaven and Earth tolerate you!"

units.zh: 友珪曰：「老賊萬段！」
units.en: Yougui cried: "Old thief, ten thousand cuts!"
units.literal: Yougui said: "Old villain, ten thousand cuts!"

units.zh: 友珪僕夫馮廷諤刺帝腹，刃出於背。
units.en: Yougui's groom Feng Tingyu drove a blade into the Emperor's belly until it showed at his back.
units.literal: Yougui’s servant Feng Tingyu stabbed the Emperor in the belly; the blade came out his back.

units.zh: 友珪自以敗氈裹之，瘞於寢殿，秘不發喪。
units.en: Yougui himself wrapped the body in a cast-off rug, buried it in the hall, and concealed the death.
units.literal: Yougui himself wrapped the corpse in a worn rug, buried it in the sleeping hall, and kept the death secret.

units.zh: 遣供奉官丁昭溥馳詣東都，命均王友貞殺友文。
units.en: He sent palace attendant Ding Zhaopu in haste to the Eastern Capital to order Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.
units.literal: He dispatched Palace Attendant Ding Zhaopu posthaste to the Eastern Capital ordering Prince of Jun Youzhen to kill Youwen.

units.zh: 己卯，矯詔稱：「博王友文謀逆，遣兵突入殿中，賴郢王友珮忠孝，將兵誅之，保全朕躬。
units.en: On jimao a forged edict read: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted revolt and burst into the hall with troops; Prince of Ying Yougui, loyal and filial, led forces to execute them and saved Us.
units.literal: On jimao a forged edict stated: "Prince of Bo Youwen plotted rebellion and sent troops bursting into the hall; thanks to Prince of Ying Yougui’s loyalty and filial piety, who led troops to execute them and preserved Our person.

units.zh: 然疾因震驚，彌致危殆，宜令友珪權主軍國之務。」
units.en: Shock has worsened Our illness—let Yougui govern state and army affairs for now."
units.literal: Yet the illness from shock grows critical—let Yougui provisionally direct state and military affairs."

units.zh: 韓勍為友珪謀，多出府庫金帛，賜諸軍及百官以取悅。
units.en: Han Qin schemed for him, emptying much gold and silk from the treasury to buy the armies and the officials.
units.literal: Han Qin plotted for Yougui, taking much gold and silk from the treasury to bestow on the armies and the hundred officials to win favor.

units.zh: 辛巳，丁昭溥還，聞友文已死，乃發喪，宣遺制，友珪即皇帝位。
units.en: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; learning Youwen was dead, they announced mourning, proclaimed the testament, and Yougui seized the throne.
units.literal: On xinsi Ding Zhaopu returned; hearing Youwen was already dead, they then announced the mourning, proclaimed the testamentary order, and Yougui at once took the throne.

units.zh: 友珪葬太祖于伊闕縣，號宣陵。
units.en: Yougui buried Taizu at Yique, naming the tomb Xuan.
units.literal: Yougui buried Taizu in Yique County, titled the tomb Xuan Mausoleum.

units.zh: 《五代史補》：太祖硃全忠，黃巢之先鋒。
units.en: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Taizu Zhu Quanzhong was Huang Chao's vanguard.
units.literal: 《Supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties》: Taizu Zhu Quanzhong was vanguard of Huang Chao.

units.zh: 巢入長安，以刺史王鐸圍同州，太祖遂降，鐸承制拜同州刺史。
units.en: When Chao took Chang'an, Wang Duo besieged Tongzhou; Taizu surrendered, and Duo, with imperial warrant, made him prefect of Tong.
units.literal: When Chao entered Chang’an, Wang Duo besieged Tongzhou; Taizu then surrendered and Duo, acting on imperial order, appointed him prefect of Tong.

units.zh: 黃巢滅，淮、蔡間秦宗權復盛，朝廷以淮、蔡與汴州相接，太祖汴人，必究其能否，遂移授宣武軍節度使以討宗權，未凡滅之。
units.en: After Huang Chao fell, Qin Zongquan rose again between Huai and Cai; because those regions marched with Bian and Taizu was a native of Bian, the court had to try him and transferred him as Xuanwu commissioner to destroy Zongquan—which he soon did.
units.literal: When Huang Chao was destroyed, Qin Zongquan revived his strength between Huai and Cai; the court, because Huai and Cai bordered Bianzhou and Taizu was a man of Bian, was bound to test his ability, and so transferred him as Xuanwu Military Commissioner to attack Zongquan; before long he destroyed him.

units.zh: 自是威福由己，朝廷不能制，遂有天下。
units.en: Thereafter he held power in his own hands and the court could not restrain him until he possessed the realm.
units.literal: From then on power and favor were his own and the court could not control him; he then possessed the realm.

units.zh: 先是，民間傳讖曰：「五公符」，又謂之「李淳風轉天歌」，其字有「八牛之年」，識者以「八牛」乃「硃」字，則太祖革命之應焉。
units.en: Earlier folk prophecy spoke of "Five Lords' tally," also called Li Chunfeng's Turning Heaven Song, containing "the year of eight oxen"—readers saw eight oxen as the character Zhu, presaging Taizu's rise.
units.literal: Earlier the people had transmitted a prophecy saying "Five Lords tally," also called the "Li Chunfeng Turning Heaven Song"; its characters had "the year of eight oxen"—those who understood took "eight oxen" as the character Zhu—thus the omen of Taizu’s revolution.

units.zh: 太祖之用兵也，法令嚴峻，每戰，逐隊主帥或有沒而不反者，其餘皆斬之，謂之：「跋隊斬」。
units.en: Taizu's armies were ruled by harsh law: when a unit commander fell and did not return, his whole unit was beheaded—this was called "beheading the straggler."
units.literal: In Taizu’s use of troops the laws were stern; in each battle if a unit commander was lost and did not return, the rest were all beheaded—called "beheading the straggling unit."

units.zh: 自是戰無不勝。
units.en: From then on his battles knew no defeat.
units.literal: From then on in battle there was no not winning.

units.zh: 然健兒且多竄匿州郡，疲於追捕，因下令文面，健兒文面自此始也。
units.en: Yet able men often hid among the prefectures, exhausted from pursuit—so he ordered facial brands, and the branding of strong soldiers began.
units.literal: Yet strong soldiers often hid in prefectures and counties, weary of pursuit; therefore he ordered facial tattooing—facial tattooing of strong soldiers began here.

units.zh: 《五代史闕文》：世傳梁太祖迎昭宗於鳳翔，素服待罪，昭宗佯為鞋系脫，呼梁祖曰：「全忠為吾系鞋。」
units.en: 《Lost Passages》: Tradition says that when Liang Taizu welcomed Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang, he wore plain dress to await punishment; Zhaozong feigned a loose shoe-thong and called: "Quanzhong, tie my shoe for me."
units.literal: 《Lost Passages of the History of the Five Dynasties》: The world transmits that when Liang Taizu welcomed Emperor Zhaozong from Fengxiang, in plain clothes he awaited punishment; Zhaozong pretended his shoe thong came loose and called Liang Taizu: "Quanzhong, tie my shoe for me."

units.zh: 梁祖不得已，跪而結之，汗流浹背。
units.en: Liang Taizu could only kneel to tie it, sweat soaking his back.
units.literal: Liang Taizu had no choice but to kneel and tie it; sweat streamed down his back.

units.zh: 時天子扈蹕尚有衛兵，昭宗意謂左右擒梁祖以殺之，其如無敢動者。
units.en: The Son of Heaven's escort still had guards; Zhaozong hoped those beside him would seize Taizu and kill him—yet none dared.
units.literal: At that time the Son of Heaven’s progress still had guard troops; Zhaozong’s intent was that those beside him seize Liang Taizu and kill him—but none dared move.

units.zh: 自是梁祖被召多不至，盡去昭宗禁衛，皆用汴人矣。
units.en: Thereafter Taizu often ignored summons; he stripped Zhaozong of every palace guard and replaced them with men from Bian.
units.literal: From then on when Liang Taizu was summoned he often did not come; he removed all Zhaozong’s forbidden guards and used only men of Bian.

units.zh: 臣謹案：梁祖以天復三年迎唐昭宗於岐下，歲在甲子，其年改天祐，至國初建隆庚申歲，才五十六年矣，然則乾德七十歲人皆目睹其事。
units.en: This commentator notes: Liang Taizu in Tianfu year 3 welcomed Tang Emperor Zhaozong from below Qi in the jiazi year, then Tianyou; from Jianlong's founding gengshen to our day is only fifty-six years—yet men of seventy in the Qiande era saw it with their own eyes.
units.literal: Your servant respectfully notes: Liang Taizu in the third year of Tianfu welcomed Tang Emperor Zhaozong from below Qi—year jiazi; that year was changed to Tianyou; from the founding of the state in the gengshen year of Jianlong it was only fifty-six years—yet people of the Qiande era, seventy years old, all witnessed the affair.

units.zh: 蓋唐室自懿宗失政，天下亂離，故武宗以下實錄，不傳於世。
units.en: From Tang Yizong's loss of rule the realm shattered; veritable records from Wuzong down no longer circulated.
units.literal: It is that from Emperor Yizong of Tang the government was lost and the realm torn apart; therefore veritable records from Emperor Wuzong down were not transmitted in the world.

units.zh: 昭宗一朝，全無記注。
units.en: Zhaozong's entire reign left no record whatsoever.
units.literal: For Zhaozong’s entire reign there was no record at all.

units.zh: 梁祖在位止及六年，均帝朝詔史臣修梁祖實錄，岐下系鞋之事，恥而不書。
units.en: Taizu reigned only six years; under Emperor Jun historians were ordered to compile his veritable record—yet the shoe-tying at Qi was too shameful to write.
units.literal: Liang Taizu reigned only six years; in Emperor Jun’s reign an edict ordered historians to compile Taizu’s veritable record—the affair of tying shoes below Qi was shameful and not written.

units.zh: 晉天福中，史臣張昭重修《唐史》，始有《昭宗本紀》，但雲即位之始，有《會昌》之風，岐陽事蹟，不能追補。
units.en: In Jin's Tianfu era Zhang Zhao revised the Tang history and added Annals of Emperor Zhaozong, noting only Huichang-era style at his accession—affairs at Qi-yang could not be recovered.
units.literal: In the Tianfu era of Jin, historian Zhang Zhao revised the 《History of Tang》, and only then was there 《Annals of Emperor Zhaozong》, but it said only that at the beginning of his reign there was the style of the Huichang era; affairs at Qi-yang could not be pursued and supplemented.

units.zh: 此亦明唐昭宗有英睿之氣，而衰運不振；
units.en: This shows that Zhaozong had keen spirit, yet declining fortune would not turn;
units.literal: This also shows that Tang Emperor Zhaozong had keen and discerning spirit, yet the declining fortune did not revive;

units.zh: 又明左右無忠義奮發之臣，致梁祖得行其志。
units.en: and that none beside him were loyal enough to strike, so Taizu could do as he pleased.
units.literal: it also shows that those beside him had no loyal and righteous ministers who would rise up, so Liang Taizu could carry out his will.

units.zh: 有所警誡，不可不書。
units.en: There is a lesson here, and it must be written.
units.literal: There is warning in this—it must not go unwritten.

Same mother does not imply same birth year. Later allusions are not personal activity. Research or record a blocker rather than invent precision. A report cannot approve with missing checks or unresolved research.
